article.title: Alternancia entre términos familiares y técnicos en un sitio
article.chapter: Norma, estilo y elección avanzada C2 — 規範、文體與進階選擇 C2

claims.summary: The Taiwan government website guideline recommends consistent terms and, for specialist terminology, either explanation or familiar wording before the technical term.

A government-platform case about the Household Registration Department website reports that users did not understand some administrative labels and recommends replacing 同胎次序 with 出生順序 and clarifying parent-related distinctions with familiar words.

The cited case illustrates a local shift from administrative vocabulary to familiar labels and explanatory wording within the same service page; it is a scoped interpretation of the described redesign, not a claim of synonymy.
The guideline and case concern public-facing government website content and do not establish universal within-document academic/casual register alternation across genres or contexts.

links.notes: Guideline explicitly says use consistent terminology, explain specialist terms or use familiar language first then add the term, and avoid rare/difficult words.

locator.section: 網站使用痛點與需求分析; 優化項目 4

links.notes: Government case identifies jargon as a barrier and recommends the familiar label 出生順序 and explicit mother/father distinctions.
The recommendation places familiar wording and a technical term together within public website content.

locator.section: 優化項目 4; 設計結果

links.notes: The case documents an actual proposed combination of familiar labels and additional explanation for the same service.
Guideline scope is government website services and their user-facing content.
